security_audit.summary: The skill is legitimate Windows BusyBox setup guidance. It asks agents or users to run PowerShell and download executables from hardcoded external URLs. I confirmed the shell and download risks, dismissed documentation-only links and simple local usage examples, and found no evidence of prompt injection.

remediation.suggestion: Pin exact BusyBox release versions and require checksum or signature verification before saving or running downloaded binaries.
Require explicit user approval before running any PowerShell command and explain each command before execution.
Make the registry metadata check optional or replace it with a less sensitive OS version check where possible.
Prefer a trusted package manager or official release channel with integrity metadata instead of bare executable URLs.

content.user_title: Run BusyBox Unix Tools on Windows
content.value_statement: Windows environments often lack common Unix command line tools. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code install and use Win32 BusyBox.
actual_capabilities: Explains that the skill is intended only for Windows environments.
Provides PowerShell commands to inspect CPU and Windows version details.
Lists BusyBox download options for 32-bit x86, 64-bit x86, Unicode, and ARM builds.
Shows how to list available BusyBox applets after installation.
Explains that Unix-style commands should be prefixed with busybox.exe.
Links to BusyBox documentation and the original BusyBox project.
limitations: It is not useful on Unix or Linux systems.
It depends on external BusyBox builds hosted outside the skill repository.
It does not provide checksum or signature verification steps.
It does not configure PATH entries or shell aliases.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Windows Developer Workstation
use_cases.description: Install a compact set of Unix-style command line utilities on a Windows machine.

use_cases.title: Standardize Script Helpers
use_cases.description: Use one BusyBox binary to provide common commands for local scripts and troubleshooting.

use_cases.title: Support Cross-Platform Commands
use_cases.description: Help users translate simple Unix command examples for Windows environments.

prompt_templates.title: Check Windows Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to decide whether BusyBox is appropriate for my Windows workstation. Explain prerequisites before any command is run.

prompt_templates.title: Install BusyBox Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through installing the right BusyBox build on Windows. Ask before running PowerShell and include verification steps if available.

prompt_templates.title: Use Unix Commands
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to run common Unix-style commands through BusyBox on Windows, using safe read-only examples first.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Team Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a secure rollout plan for BusyBox on Windows workstations, including trusted sourcing, integrity verification, and usage conventions.

output_examples.input: I need Unix-style tools on a Windows laptop.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the system is Windows, identifies the correct build family, and asks before any download command is run.

output_examples.input: Help me use BusyBox after installation.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains how to list available tools and how to prefix commands with the BusyBox executable.

output_examples.input: Prepare this for a team image.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends a trusted source, integrity verification, version pinning, and a documented usage convention.

best_practices: Confirm the environment is Windows before using the skill.
Verify downloaded executables with checksums or signatures before use.
Review each PowerShell command before approving execution.
anti_patterns: Running a downloaded BusyBox executable without integrity verification.
Executing PowerShell commands automatically without user approval.
Using this skill on Unix or Linux systems where BusyBox is already native.

faq.question: What does this skill install?
faq.answer: It guides installation of a Win32 BusyBox executable that provides many Unix-style command line utilities.

faq.question: Does it work on Linux or macOS?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly targets Windows and tells Unix users to stop.

faq.question: Does it need PowerShell?
faq.answer: Yes. The setup instructions use PowerShell commands for system checks and downloads.

faq.question: Are downloads verified?
faq.answer: No. The skill does not include checksum or signature verification.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. It declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users approve manually?
faq.answer: Users should approve all shell commands and any executable download before the agent runs them.
